requirements.text: ctx-execute-enforcer allows Bash from vbw:* agents and bare vbw CLI calls, while still blocking the main thread, other agents, and compound vbw commands

with only VBW 1 present setup.sh prints the VBW 1 detection line as before and no VBW 2 line
with both present setup.sh reports both
with neither present setup.sh reports VBW absent
with several VBW 2 versions cached the reported version is the one Claude Code loads (active entry, else highest)

main-thread behaviour of grep-cmm-gate, cmm-grep-nudge and cmm-nudge is unchanged
session-gate either allows a vbw:* agent or names a wrapper call that, once run, lifts the block; with no wrapper installed it does not hold the agent
session-gate does not hold a vbw:* agent for the Context Mode sentinel; the main thread still is

requirements.text: A VBW 2 agent can run CMM queries (search_graph, trace_path, get_code_snippet, search_code) within its tool allowlist and get results

rules.text: the wrapper runs the allowed read tools and index_repository as codebase-memory-mcp cli --quiet <tool>, keeping the caller's arguments
any other tool name, or none, exits non-zero listing the allowed tools without calling CMM
the project is resolved from cwd with project-root.sh (subdirectory and superproject) and injected; index_repository gets repo_path
codebase-memory-mcp missing from PATH exits non-zero with one line naming the fix
an unindexed project is reported as such with the index_repository wrapper command
malformed JSON arguments exit non-zero with an error, never an empty result
a successful index_repository writes the session-ready sentinel and clears the indexing marker; a failed one writes none
VBW 2's guard-bash.jq with a run open does not refuse a wrapper call, index_repository included
search_graph, trace_path, get_code_snippet and search_code via the wrapper return results in an indexed fixture repo (visible SKIP without the CMM binary)
setup.sh installs the wrapper and its libs when VBW 2 is detected and not otherwise; --uninstall removes it
a plain wrapper call passes ctx-execute-enforcer for the main thread and vbw:* agents and passes ctx-payload-guard; piped or redirected wrapper calls stay blocked for the main thread

phases.title: Unblock VBW 2 runs: enforcer exemption and VBW 2 detection
phases.goal: VBW 2 workflow agents and bare vbw CLI calls pass ctx-execute-enforcer, and setup.sh identifies a VBW 2 install as distinct from VBW 1 and prints its version.
criteria: ctx-execute-enforcer exits 0 for Bash with agent_type matching vbw:* (any command, compound included, e.g. agent_type vbw:dev `pytest`, agent_type vbw:qa `cd x && mypy`), checked before compound-shell normalization; the exemption is keyed on the PreToolUse input's agent_type field
Bare vbw calls exit 0 from any caller: `vbw show contract`, `VBW_SESSION_ID=abc vbw next --json`, `/abs/path/vbw prove`

Still blocked (exit 2): main-thread `pytest`; agent_type Explore `cat`; general-purpose agent large-output commands; `vbw next | jq`, `vbw x && cat`, `vbw x; y`, `vbw decide $(cat f)`, a backtick substitution, `vbw x > f`; `vbwx foo` (name-prefix lookalike)
Missing, empty or malformed agent_type falls through to the normal enforcement path (no exemption, no crash)
Each exemption is logged through track-hook-blocks.sh with a distinct reason (vbw-agent, vbw-cli)
Existing VBW 1 allowlist entries (`*/.vbw-planning/*`, `/tmp/.vbw-plugin-root-link-*`) keep their current behavior
A new or extended tests/test-*.sh covers all 11 field cases from worker-simulator todo c4e1b7a2 plus the `;`, backtick and redirect cases, and passes under `make test`

hooks/lib/vbw-source.sh returns a VBW 2 source type distinct from VBW 1 types when the plugin cache holds vbw-marketplace/vbw/2.x (and/or a `vbw` CLI on PATH), and exposes the version read from the plugin's VERSION file

setup.sh prints a line naming VBW 2 and its version (e.g. 2.1.18) when VBW 2 is installed; prints VBW 1 detection as before when only VBW 1 is present; reports both when both are present; reports absent when neither
With multiple VBW 2 versions in the plugin cache, the reported version is the one Claude Code loads (highest/active), and the choice is covered by a test
Detection tests use fixture plugin trees in mktemp dirs (no dependency on the developer's real install) and pass under `make test`

phases.title: A permitted CMM route for VBW 2 agents: CLI wrapper and gate audit
phases.goal: A vbw:* agent can query the CMM graph through Bash with its existing tool allowlist, and every stack gate either allows it or names that exact working command.
criteria: setup.sh installs a CMM wrapper command (per D2) when VBW 2 is detected; uninstall removes it; it is listed in stack-owned files and covered by CHECKSUMS.sha256 if under a checksummed tree

Wrapper accepts search_graph, trace_path, get_code_snippet, search_code (plus the other read tools: query_graph, get_architecture, list_projects/index_status) and index_repository; any other tool name (e.g. delete_project) exits non-zero with a message listing allowed tools

Wrapper resolves the CMM project from cwd using the shared hooks/lib/project-root.sh logic (monorepo/superproject root), injects it so the agent need not pass project, and always passes --quiet to `codebase-memory-mcp cli`
Wrapper errors clearly (non-zero, one-line message naming the fix) when codebase-memory-mcp is not on PATH; when the project is not indexed it says so and names the index_repository wrapper command
Malformed JSON args yield a non-zero exit and an error message, never a silent empty result

Each of search_graph, trace_path, get_code_snippet and search_code run via the wrapper from a Bash call in an indexed fixture repo returns non-empty results (test under make test, skipped with a visible SKIP when the CMM binary is absent)
A wrapper call, including index_repository, is not refused by VBW 2's guard-bash.jq while a vbw run is open (verified live in a vbw run, or by feeding the guard its input with run-open set)
Wrapper call passes ctx-execute-enforcer and ctx-payload-guard for vbw:* agents and the main thread

grep-cmm-gate (per D1): code-file Grep from a vbw:* agent exits 2 with a message containing the exact wrapper command line to run instead; non-code Grep (configs, docs, .vbw/) is allowed; exits 0 (fail-open) when the CMM CLI is missing or the repo is unindexed
cmm-nudge on Read stays advisory for vbw:* agents (exit 0) and its message names the wrapper command, not MCP tool names

session-gate: a vbw:* agent is never blocked waiting for a sentinel it cannot create with its tools; either it is allowed or the block message names a wrapper call that satisfies the gate, and a test proves that call lifts the block

agent-cmm-gate: an Agent call with subagent_type vbw:* is not blocked for lacking a CMM keyword in a way the caller cannot satisfy; workflow-spawned vbw:* agents (spawned via workflow ask, no Agent tool call) are documented as not passing through this gate
Main-thread and non-VBW agent behavior of all four gates is unchanged (existing tests still pass)
Tests for each gate with agent_type vbw:* inputs pass under make test

phases.title: Actionable CMM-first guidance for all 7 VBW 2 agents and CMM-backed mapping
phases.goal: Every VBW 2 agent type is told, at start, how to search code via the CMM wrapper with tools it actually has, and vbw map produces a map.md that points later agents at the live CMM graph.
criteria: subagent-cmm-startup.sh (SubagentStart) detects agent_type vbw:architect, vbw:lead, vbw:dev, vbw:qa, vbw:scout, vbw:debugger, vbw:docs and emits additionalContext containing the exact wrapper command lines for search_graph, trace_path, get_code_snippet and search_code with this repo's resolved project
Guidance for vbw:* agents names no MCP tool calls (no mcp__ names, no ctx_execute) since their allowlists lack them; non-VBW agents keep their current guidance
Guidance tells agents when Grep/Read is still right (literals, non-code files, configs) consistent with grep-cmm-gate's rules from P2
When the CMM CLI is missing or the repo is unindexed, vbw:* guidance says so and gives the index_repository wrapper command or omits CMM advice; it never instructs a command that will fail
A test feeds SubagentStart JSON for each of the 7 agent types and asserts the wrapper command appears and no mcp__ name appears
vbw:scout guidance during mapping instructs scouts to take structure (architecture, entry points, call relationships) from get_architecture/search_graph via the wrapper before reading files

After a `vbw map` run on an indexed repo, .vbw/map.md contains a section naming the CMM project and the wrapper command for querying the live graph (verified by grep on the produced file), landing in a section the mapping.js MAP schema allows
A recorded vbw map run's scout transcripts (subagents/workflows/<run>/*.jsonl) contain at least one wrapper CMM call per scout angle
agent-override-generate.sh does not generate .claude/agents/vbw-*.md overrides for a VBW 2-only install (they target agent names VBW 2 never spawns), while VBW 1 installs are unaffected

decisions.text: vbw:* enforcement posture: Redirect (grep-cmm-gate blocks code Grep from vbw:* and names the exact codebase-memory-mcp cli command; fails open when CLI missing or repo unindexed; Read stays advisory)
decisions.why: Same rules as main thread and R4 holds; accepts a turn per blocked Grep and that Bash rg still bypasses

decisions.text: CMM CLI access for vbw:* agents: setup.sh installs a wrapper command that enforces a read-tool allowlist plus index_repository, resolves the project from cwd and adds --quiet; agents may index when the project is missing; SessionStart keeps kicking off indexing (existing hook-driven indexing on develop)
decisions.why: User's choice: shorter agent commands and one place for project lookup, works on never-indexed repos; accepts one more installed file that can drift from CMM CLI flags and agents writing graphs

decisions.text: Upstream proposal (old R7/R8) moved to next milestone, after a field test on a large multi-sub-project repo; private-repo evidence anonymized
decisions.why: User wants better evidence before filing upstream

decisions.why: No contributor loses a path; accepts two processes to keep in step
